messages.content:
Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The ants cannot pass each other, so their left-to-right order is preserved. Simulating the collisions:

- A (10, +3) and B (40, -1) meet at \(t = \frac{40-10}{3+1} = 7.5\) s at position 32.5 cm. They reverse: A moves left at 3, B moves right at 1.
- At \(t=7.5\), C is at \(80 - 2(7.5) = 65\) cm moving left at 2.
- A then travels left from 32.5 cm to 0, falling at \(t = 7.5 + \frac{32.5}{3} = \frac{55}{3}\) s.
- B (now right at 1) and C (left at 2) meet after \(\frac{65-32.5}{1+2} = \frac{65}{6}\) s, i.e. at \(t = 7.5 + \frac{65}{6} = \frac{55}{3}\) s, exactly when A falls. Their collision position is \(32.5 + 1\cdot\frac{65}{6} = \frac{130}{3}\) cm. They reverse: B moves left at 1, C moves right at 2.
- After this, B falls off the left end at \(t = \frac{55}{3} + \frac{130/3}{1} = \frac{185}{3}\) s.
- C falls off the right end at \(t = \frac{55}{3} + \frac{100 - 130/3}{2} = \frac{140}{3}\) s.

The last ant (B) falls at \(\frac{185}{3}\) seconds.

ANSWER: 185/3
